newsitem.title: USA: Scab found in southern Illinois SRW wheat - tour.
newsitem.headline: Scab found in southern Illinois SRW wheat - tour.

text.p: Participants on one route during the second day of the annual soft red winter wheat tour said they were seeing minimal to moderate disease effects of fusarium head scab in many wheat fields.
Signs of scab, a fungus that attacks the wheat head in the developing kernel, were seen in several fields in southern Illinois, scouts on the Wheat Quality Council-sponsored tour said.
"This could affect feed set and quality," said Jerry Rauch, marketing agronomist with Hybritech Seed International, a unit of Monsanto Co.
"But we tend to be optimistic about yields," Rauch said.
His car had made five stops in Effingham, Fayette, Marion counties, all in southern Illinois.

Rauch's group calculated an estimated yield of about 45 bushels per acre from a range of 38.3 to 60 bushels. That compares to an average yield of 32 bushels per acre in 1996 and 51 bushels in 1995 from counties in southeast Illinois according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
Other problems seen were barley yellow dwarf, a disease carried by aphids that affects grain quality, rust and tan spot.
"These diseases are present but not necessarily causing physiological damage to the plant," Rauch said.
Jim Quinton, grain merchandiser with Consolidated Grain and Barge, said he was also finding evidence of scab. His vehicle had visited five counties in southern Illinois.
Reached by cellphone, tour leader Quinton said "the scab is very light and not in epidemic proportions."
On the crop tour's second day, 60 participants in 15 vehicles were scouting four crop-reporting districts in southern Illinois. The tour decided to bypass Kentucky because of time concerns.
The tour ends Wednesday in Little Rock, Ark.
